# 12-Week Hypertrophy Programme for a 26-Year-Old Recreational Female Lifter (Vegan)

Below is a periodised 12-week muscle gain plan, structured as three 4-week mesocycles with progressive overload, deload waves, and a fully plant-based nutrition protocol hitting 150 g protein/day.

---

## Programme Overview

- **Training split:** 4 days/week Upper/Lower (Weeks 1–4), shifting to a 5-day Push/Pull/Legs + Upper/Lower hybrid (Weeks 5–12) once work capacity improves.
- **Rep ranges:** 6–15 reps with RIR (Reps in Reserve) progression — start at RIR 3, end mesocycles at RIR 0–1.
- **Cardio:** 2× weekly low-intensity (Zone 2, 20–30 min) for recovery and cardiovascular health, kept low to preserve surplus.
- **Recovery:** 7–9 hrs sleep, 1 full rest day, mobility work daily (10 min).

---

## PHASE 1: Foundation & Volume Accumulation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Build technique, baseline volume, and tendon resilience. 4 days/week, Upper/Lower split.

### Weekly Layout
- **Mon:** Upper A
- **Tue:** Lower A
- **Wed:** Rest / Zone 2 cardio
- **Thu:** Upper B
- **Fri:** Lower B
- **Sat:** Optional Zone 2 cardio + mobility
- **Sun:** Rest

### Upper A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RIR |
|---|---|---|
| Barbell bench press | 3 × 8 | 3 |
| One-arm DB row | 3 × 10 each | 3 |
| Seated DB shoulder press | 3 × 10 | 3 |
| Lat pulldown | 3 × 12 | 2 |
| Cable triceps pushdown | 2 × 12 | 2 |
| DB hammer curl | 2 × 12 | 2 |

### Lower A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RIR |
|---|---|---|
| Back squat | 3 × 8 | 3 |
| Romanian deadlift | 3 × 10 | 3 |
| Walking DB lunge | 3 × 10 each | 2 |
| Leg curl | 3 × 12 | 2 |
| Standing calf raise | 3 × 15 | 2 |
| Hanging knee raise | 3 × 10 | 2 |

### Upper B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RIR |
|---|---|---|
| Incline DB press | 3 × 10 | 3 |
| Chest-supported row | 3 × 10 | 3 |
| Lateral raise | 3 × 15 | 2 |
| Cable face pull | 3 × 15 | 2 |
| Incline DB curl | 2 × 12 | 2 |
| Overhead cable triceps extension | 2 × 12 | 2 |

### Lower B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RIR |
|---|---|---|
| Conventional deadlift | 3 × 6 | 3 |
| Leg press | 3 × 12 | 2 |
| DB Bulgarian split squat | 3 × 10 each | 2 |
| Hip thrust | 3 × 12 | 2 |
| Seated calf raise | 3 × 15 | 2 |
| Cable crunch | 3 × 12 | 2 |

**Weekly progression (Weeks 1–4):**
- Week 1: Learn loads, RIR 3.
- Week 2: Add 2.5–5 lb to compounds; RIR 2.
- Week 3: Add another increment; RIR 1–2.
- Week 4: **Deload** — same exercises, 2 sets each, 60% load, RIR 4. Focus on tempo and contraction.

---

## PHASE 2: Intensification & Volume Expansion (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** Increase weekly volume per muscle, push closer to failure, introduce more isolation. Shift to 5 days/week.

### Weekly Layout
- **Mon:** Push
- **Tue:** Pull
- **Wed:** Legs
- **Thu:** Rest / Zone 2 cardio
- **Fri:** Upper (hypertrophy focus)
- **Sat:** Lower (glute/ham focus)
- **Sun:** Rest

|---|---|---|
| Incline barbell bench | 4 × 6–8 | 2 |
| Flat DB press | 3 × 10 | 2 |
| Seated machine shoulder press | 3 × 10 | 2 |
| Cable lateral raise | 4 × 12–15 | 1 |
| Cable chest fly | 3 × 12 | 1 |
| Rope triceps pushdown | 3 × 12 | 1 |
| Overhead DB triceps extension | 2 × 12 | 1 |

### Pull (back, rear delts, biceps)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RIR |
|---|---|---|
| Pull-up (assisted as needed) | 4 × AMRAP @ RIR 1 | 1 |
| Barbell row | 3 × 8 | 2 |
| Seated cable row | 3 × 10 | 2 |
| Straight-arm lat pulldown | 3 × 12 | 1 |
| Reverse pec deck | 3 × 15 | 1 |
| EZ-bar curl | 3 × 10 | 1 |
| Cable curl | 2 × 12 | 1 |

### Legs (quad + posterior balance)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RIR |
|---|---|---|
| Back squat | 4 × 6–8 | 2 |
| Romanian deadlift | 3 × 8 | 2 |
| Leg press | 3 × 12 | 1 |
| Leg curl | 4 × 12 | 1 |

### Upper (hypertrophy)

### Lower (glute/ham focus)

| Hanging leg raise | 3 × 10 | 1 |

**Weekly progression:**
- Week 5: New split, RIR 2.
- Week 6: Add a set to weakest lagging muscle (typically delts or back); RIR 1–2.
- Week 7: Push RIR 0–1 on isolation; maintain RIR 1–2 on compounds.
- Week 8: **Deload** — cut volume by 40%, RIR 4, reduce sessions to 3.

---

## PHASE 3: Peak Hypertrophy & Specialisation (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** Maximise stimulus on lagging areas (commonly delts/back/glutes for a female recreational lifter), train very close to failure, introduce intensifiers.

### Weekly Layout: Same 5-day structure, but with **intensity techniques**:
- 1 drop set on the final set of one isolation lift per session
- Myo-reps on lateral raises and leg curls
- Cluster sets on the main compound (e.g., 5 × 3 with 20s rest at 80%)

### Sample upgraded **Push** day (Week 9–11)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Incline barbell bench | 4 × 6 | RIR 1 |
| Flat DB press | 3 × 8–10 | RIR 1 |
| Machine shoulder press | 3 × 10 | RIR 0 last set |
| Cable lateral raise — myo-reps | 1 × 15 + 4 × 5 mini-sets | To failure |
| Pec deck | 3 × 12 + drop on last set | RIR 0 |
| Rope pushdown | 3 × 12 | RIR 0 |

Apply the same intensification logic to Pull, Legs, Upper, Lower days — add one drop set, one myo-rep set, or one cluster set per session, not more (to keep recovery manageable).

**Weekly progression:**
- Week 9: Introduce intensifiers, RIR 0–1 on isolations.
- Week 10: Add one extra set to your two priority muscles.
- Week 11: Peak week — highest volume + intensity of the block.
- Week 12: **Deload + reassess** — 3 sessions, 50% volume, RIR 4. Retest key lifts (squat, bench, RDL, pull-up) at end of week.

---

## Nutrition: 150 g Plant-Based Protein/Day

Assuming ~145 lb (66 kg) bodyweight as a reasonable estimate for a recreational lifter (adjust as needed). 150 g protein = ~2.3 g/kg — well above the hypertrophy threshold, smart given lower digestibility/leucine content of plant proteins (PDCAAS adjustment).

### Caloric Target for Lean Gain
- **Surplus:** +250–350 kcal above maintenance
- **Estimated target:** ~2,300–2,500 kcal/day (adjust based on weekly weigh-ins; aim for +0.25–0.5 lb/week)
- **Macros:** 150 g protein / 280–320 g carbs / 65–75 g fat

### Daily Protein Distribution (4–5 feedings of 30–40 g each)

| Meal | Sample Food | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| Breakfast | 60 g oats + 40 g vegan protein powder (pea/soy blend) + 200 ml soy milk + berries | ~38 g |
| Lunch | 200 g tempeh or 250 g extra-firm tofu + quinoa + greens + tahini | ~38 g |
| Pre/Post-workout shake | 40 g pea+rice protein blend + banana + soy milk | ~35 g |
| Dinner | 150 g seitan or 250 g lentils + brown rice + veg + nutritional yeast (20 g) | ~40 g |
| Optional snack | Edamame (1 cup) + soy yogurt | ~20 g |

### Key Plant Protein Sources (rank by quality)
1. **Soy** (tofu, tempeh, edamame, soy milk, TVP) — complete amino acid profile, high leucine. **Use daily.**
2. **Seitan** — very high protein (~25 g/100 g), low lysine — pair with legumes.
3. **Lentils & beans** — pair with rice/quinoa for complete profile.
4. **Pea + rice protein powder blend** — closest plant analog to whey for leucine. Aim for 2–3 g leucine per dose (≈30–40 g protein).
5. **Nutritional yeast, hemp seeds, pumpkin seeds** — protein top-ups.

### Critical Supplements for Vegan Lifters
- **Vitamin B12:** 250 mcg/day (non-negotiable)
- **Vitamin D3 (lichen-derived):** 1000–2000 IU/day
- **Algae-based omega-3 (EPA/DHA):** 500 mg/day
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 5 g/day (vegans typically have lower baseline stores — this is one of the highest-value supplements for her)
- **Iron and zinc:** monitor via bloodwork at week 1 and week 12; supplement only if low
- **Iodine:** ½ tsp iodised salt daily or kelp-based supplement

---

## Recovery & Lifestyle Protocols

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours; consistent bed/wake time.
- **Mobility:** 10 min daily (hips, t-spine, ankles).
- **Stress management:** 1 yoga or walking session/week.
- **Tracking:** Log all lifts; aim to add reps or weight session-to-session within each 4-week block.
- **Weekly check-in:** Bodyweight average (5–7 morning weigh-ins), waist measurement, 1 progress photo. Adjust calories ±150 kcal if scale stalls or jumps too fast.

---

## Expected Outcomes (12 Weeks)

- **Bodyweight:** +4–7 lb (mostly lean tissue with surplus dialled in)
- **Strength:** ~15–25% improvement on main compounds
- **Visible hypertrophy:** Most notable in glutes, quads, shoulders, and back if priority work is consistent

Let me know her starting lifts, bodyweight, and any joint history and I'll fine-tune loads and exercise selection.

# Cardio Addition to the 12-Week Hypertrophy Programme

Cardio is built in to **support recovery, work capacity, and cardiovascular health without compromising the muscle gain stimulus or the caloric surplus**. Volume and intensity scale alongside the training phases.

---

## Guiding Principles

- **Modality priority:** Low-impact options (incline walking, cycling, stair climber, elliptical) on most days to minimise leg fatigue. Save higher-impact work for non-leg-adjacent days.
- **Timing:** Cardio is separated from lifting by at least 6 hours where possible. If same day, **cardio after lifting**, never before lower-body sessions.
- **Intensity zones:**
  - **Zone 2:** Conversational pace, ~60–70% max HR, RPE 4–5. Builds aerobic base, aids recovery.
  - **Zone 4–5 (HIIT):** ~85–95% max HR, RPE 8–9. Short intervals only, used sparingly.
- **Fasted vs fed:** Always **fed** — she's in a surplus and we want full performance.

---

## PHASE 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Establish aerobic base, support recovery, no interference with lifting adaptations.

### Weekly Cardio Layout
- **Wed:** Zone 2, 25 min (incline walk, treadmill 4.0 mph @ 6–8% grade, or bike)
- **Sat:** Zone 2, 30 min (outdoor walk, elliptical, or easy cycle) + 10 min mobility
- **Daily:** ~7,000–8,000 steps target on non-cardio days (NEAT for general health)

### Weekly progression
- Week 1: 25 + 30 min
- Week 2: 30 + 30 min
- Week 3: 30 + 35 min
- Week 4 (deload): 20 + 20 min, easy pace

**Total cardio: ~55–70 min/week**

---

## PHASE 2: Intensification (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** Maintain aerobic base, introduce one short conditioning session for work capacity. Lifting volume has increased, so cardio stays modest.

### Weekly Cardio Layout
- **Thu (rest from lifting):** Zone 2, 30–35 min — bike, incline walk, or elliptical
- **Sat (after lower session):** Easy Zone 2, 20 min cooldown walk
- **Sun:** Optional outdoor walk, 30–45 min, very easy (active recovery)
- **One conditioning finisher** added to **Push day (Mon)** end of session:
  - **5 rounds:** 30 sec assault bike or rower hard / 90 sec easy
  - Total: ~10 min

### Weekly progression
- Week 5: Add the conditioning finisher on Push day (5 rounds)
- Week 6: 6 rounds
- Week 7: 6 rounds + extend Thu Zone 2 to 40 min
- Week 8 (deload): Drop conditioning, 2 × 20 min Zone 2 only

**Total cardio: ~80–100 min/week**

---

## PHASE 3: Peak Hypertrophy (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** Hold cardio steady — lifting intensity is peaking, so we do **not** add cardio load. Conditioning stays in for heart health and capacity.

### Weekly Cardio Layout
- **Thu:** Zone 2, 30 min
- **Sat:** Zone 2, 25 min
- **Sun:** Easy walk, 30 min (recovery)
- **Push day finisher:** 5 rounds × 30 sec on / 90 sec off (cut back slightly to preserve recovery for intensifiers)

### Weekly progression
- Week 9: As above
- Week 10: Same — prioritise lifting recovery
- Week 11 (peak): Drop conditioning finisher entirely; keep 2 × 25 min Zone 2 only
- Week 12 (deload): 2 × 20 min Zone 2, easy

**Total cardio: ~75–90 min/week**

---

---

## Practical Coaching Notes

- **If recovery suffers** (sleep poor, joint aches, lifts regressing): cut cardio first, never lifting volume.
- **If scale climbs too fast** (>0.75 lb/week): add 10–15 min Zone 2 rather than cutting calories — preserves training fuel.
- **Heart rate monitor recommended** — most recreational lifters push Zone 2 too hard. Cap her at conversational pace; if she can't speak in full sentences, slow down.
- **Caloric adjustment:** The conditioning finishers burn ~80–120 kcal. On weeks with finishers, she should add ~100 kcal (e.g., extra serving of rice or a piece of fruit) to maintain the surplus.

# Protein Powder Recommendations for a Vegan Lifter

For a vegan athlete chasing 150 g protein/day, the right protein powder isn't a luxury — it's a practical tool to hit her target without stuffing her with food volume. Here's what to look for and what to recommend.

## Why I'd Reframe "Cheat Day" as "Refeed Meal"

**Problems with a traditional cheat day:**
- A full day of unrestricted eating can easily add 2,000–4,000 surplus kcal on top of an already-surplus diet → fat gain accelerates, blunting the lean gain goal
- Reinforces a "good food / bad food" mental model, which is associated with higher rates of disordered eating in female athletes
- Often leaves her feeling sluggish, bloated, and behind on protein the next day
- For a 26-year-old female recreational lifter, the metabolic "boost" from a single high-calorie day is minimal — this is mostly a psychological tool

**What actually works:**
- A planned **high-carb refeed meal** (or two) once a week that's flexible, satisfying, and still hits her protein target
- This gives her the social/psychological flexibility of "eating what she wants" while keeping the surplus controlled

- It's the most common social/dining-out day

- **Other meals that day:** Slightly lighter, protein-focused, lower fat to make room

## Rules That Keep It Working

1. **Hit protein first.** Protein target gets met *before* the flex meal, not skipped to "save calories." This is the single most important rule.
2. **No skipping meals to "bank" calories.** Leads to overeating at the flex meal and poor training fuel.
3. **Don't drink the whole budget.** If she chooses alcohol with the flex meal, cap at 1–2 drinks — alcohol blunts MPS and recovery.
4. **One meal, not all day.** A single 1,000–1,400 kcal meal is satisfying; a full day of "off plan" eating can hit 4,000+ kcal in a vegan context (vegan junk food is calorically dense — vegan cheese, fried foods, baked goods are not "lighter").
5. **Sunday is normal.** No compensating, no extra cardio, no skipped meals. Just return to the standard plan.
6. **Honest tracking.** She doesn't need to weigh the flex meal, but a rough mental estimate keeps her aware. Use the MyFitnessPal or similar app to log it loosely.

## When to Skip the Flex Meal

- **Deload weeks (4, 8, 12):** Skip or downsize to a normal meal — training stimulus is reduced, so the refeed isn't physiologically warranted
- **If weight is climbing too fast** (>0.75 lb/week for 2 weeks): swap the flex meal for a normal dinner until rate slows
- **If she's feeling out of control around it:** This is a red flag for the binge-restrict cycle — pull the flex meal entirely and just allow ~200 kcal of "fun food" daily instead (a piece of chocolate, a cookie). Sustainable flexibility > weekly blowout.

- Adds ~500–700 kcal of refeed (useful for glycogen, leptin, psychology) instead of 2,000+ (purely fat-gain territory)
- Maintains the protein anchor → no lost training week
- Builds a sustainable relationship with food rather than a restrict/binge pattern
- Gives her social flexibility — she can go out Saturday with friends and not feel "off plan"

If she really pushes for a full unrestricted day, I'd negotiate it to once every 3–4 weeks (aligned with deload week endings) rather than weekly. Weekly unrestricted eating on a +300 kcal/day surplus will likely shift her toward more fat than muscle gain over the 12 weeks.

After Week 11's brutality, the deload is **deeper than Phase 1 or 2 deloads**.

- **3 sessions only** (Mon/Wed/Fri)
- **50% volume, 60% load, RIR 4–5**
- Focus on movement quality, tempo, contraction
- **No intensifiers**, no failure work
- Cardio: 2 × 20 min Zone 2, that's it
- Foam rolling and mobility doubled

## Critical Coaching Cues for Phase 3

**1. RIR 0 means RIR 0.** This is where most recreational lifters fail. "Hard" is not the same as failure. Failure is when the bar/dumbbell stops moving despite maximum effort. She should have at least one set per session where she genuinely cannot complete the next rep.

**2. Intensifiers stack fatigue fast.** Use them on the **last set** of an exercise, not every set. Stacking failure across every set of every exercise will tank her recovery within a week.

**3. Form before failure.** If form breaks down significantly, terminate the set — that's effective failure. Pushing past with ugly reps just adds injury risk.

**4. Track everything.** Weights, reps, and intensifier completion. Progressive overload week to week is the actual driver of growth — intensifiers are the multiplier, not the substitute.

**5. Watch for overreach signals:**
- Resting HR up 5+ bpm for 3 days
- Sleep disrupted
- Mood dropping
- Same load suddenly feels heavier
- Joint pain (not muscle soreness)

If 2+ of these show up, pull intensity back to Phase 2 levels for a week. This isn't failure — it's smart programming.

**6. Nutrition has to scale.** Phase 3 intensity demands more fuel. If she's still eating Phase 1 calories, she'll under-recover and the intensity push backfires. Confirm she's hitting +400 surplus minimum and 150 g protein daily.

---

If executed properly:
- **Strength jump on retests:** +10–15% on most lifts versus Week 8
- **Visible hypertrophy:** Most noticeable change of the entire 12 weeks happens in this phase
- **Significant fatigue accumulation** — she should feel "cooked" entering Week 12, which is exactly what the deload is for

**Volume:** 3–4 sets per compound, 3 per isolation. RIR 1–2.

### Cardio
- Mon: 5–6 round HIIT finisher (30 sec on / 90 sec off)
- Thu: Zone 2, 30–40 min
- Sat: 20 min Zone 2 cooldown
- Sun: Optional 30–45 min easy walk
- **Week 8 deload:** Drop conditioning, 2 × 20 min Zone 2

### Weekly Progression
- **W5:** New split, RIR 2, introduce conditioning finisher
- **W6:** Add a set to weakest muscle, +1 round on finisher
- **W7:** RIR 0–1 on isolation, +10 min Zone 2
- **W8:** **Deload** — 40% volume cut, 3 sessions, RIR 4

---

## PHASE 3: Peak Hypertrophy (Weeks 9–12)

### Training: 5-Day Split (same structure, max intensity)
- **Mon:** Push (intensifiers)
- **Tue:** Pull (intensifiers)
- **Wed:** Legs — quad focus (cluster sets on squat)
- **Thu:** Rest + 20 min walk
- **Fri:** Upper (rest-pause, drop sets)
- **Sat:** Lower — glute/ham focus (eccentric overload)
- **Sun:** Full rest

**Volume:** 4 sets per compound, 3–4 per isolation. RIR 0–1.

**Intensifiers used systematically:**
- Drop sets (last set of isolations)
- Myo-reps (delts, hams, lats)
- Lengthened partials (delts, hams, biceps, triceps)
- Rest-pause (chest, back)
- Cluster sets (back squat)
- 4-second eccentrics (RDL, incline press)

### Cardio
- Drop all conditioning finishers
- Thu: 30 min Zone 2
- Sat: 25 min Zone 2
- Sun: 30 min easy walk
- **Week 11 peak:** One 20 min walk only
- **Week 12 deload:** 2 × 20 min Zone 2

### Weekly Progression
- **W9:** Introduce intensifiers, RIR 0–1 on isolations
- **W10:** +1 set to two priority muscles (delts, glutes typically)
- **W11:** **Peak week** — every isolation past failure, +500 cal surplus, 9 hr sleep
- **W12:** **Hard deload + retest** — 3 sessions, 50% volume, RIR 4, test 3RMs on key lifts

---

## Nutrition: Full 12-Week Framework

### Daily Targets
- **Protein:** 150 g (~2.3 g/kg) — non-negotiable, anchors the entire plan
- **Carbs:** 280–320 g (scaling up in Phase 3 to ~350 g)
- **Fat:** 65–75 g
- **Calories:** 2,300–2,500 (Phases 1–2), 2,500–2,700 (Phase 3)

### Protein Distribution (4–5 feedings of 30–40 g)

| Meal | Protein | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Breakfast | 35–40 g | Tofu scramble, oats + protein powder, overnight oats |
| Lunch | 35–40 g | Tempeh/tofu + grain bowl, lentil pasta, seitan stir-fry |
| Pre/post workout | 30–40 g | Pea+rice protein shake with banana + oats |
| Dinner | 35–40 g | Tofu/tempeh/seitan + carb + veg |
| Optional snack | 15–20 g | Edamame, soy yogurt, protein shake |

### Core Plant Protein Sources (Daily Rotation)
1. **Soy daily** (tofu, tempeh, edamame, soy milk) — best leucine profile
2. **Seitan** 2–3×/week — highest protein density
3. **Lentils/beans** paired with rice/quinoa — fibre + complete amino acids
4. **Pea + rice protein powder** — 1–2 scoops/day

### Recommended Supplements
- **Vitamin B12:** 250 mcg daily *(non-negotiable for vegans)*
- **Vitamin D3 (lichen-derived):** 1000–2000 IU daily
- **Algae-based omega-3 EPA/DHA:** 500 mg daily
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 5 g daily *(especially valuable — vegans have lower baseline stores)*
- **Iron + zinc:** monitor via bloodwork at W1 and W12
- **Iodine:** ½ tsp iodised salt daily

### Protein Powder Recommendation
**Top pick: Vega Sport Premium Protein** — 30 g protein, 2.7 g leucine per scoop, NSF Certified for Sport. Single scoop hits MPS threshold.

**Backup: Naked Pea** for clean ingredient preference.

Use 1–2 scoops/day max — rest of protein from whole foods.

### Weekly Flex Meal (Saturday Evening)
- **Not** a "cheat day" — a single planned high-carb meal
- **Total Saturday calories:** maintenance + 500–700 kcal
- **Protein still hits 150 g** (anchor rule)
- Flex meal itself: ~1,000–1,400 kcal, her choice
- Examples: vegan pizza, Thai takeout, loaded nachos, Beyond burger + fries
- **Skip on deload weeks** (W4, W8, W12)

---

## Sample Day Structures

### Training Day (Mon–Wed–Fri pattern)
| Time | Meal | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| 7am | Power oats bowl (oats, soy milk, pea protein, PB, berries) | 38 g |
| 12pm | Tempeh + quinoa bowl with greens | 38 g |
| 4pm | Pre-workout: banana + small shake (15 g) | 15 g |
| 5–6:30pm | **TRAIN** | — |
| 7pm | Post-workout: recovery shake (pea/rice + soy milk + banana + oats) | 40 g |
| 9pm | Dinner: seitan stir-fry + rice + veg | 35 g |
| **Total** | | **~166 g** |

### Rest Day
| Time | Meal | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| 8am | Tofu scramble + toast + avocado | 36 g |
| 12pm | Lentil pasta with marinara + tempeh "bolognese" | 45 g |
| 4pm | Edamame + soy yogurt snack | 20 g |
| 7pm | Black bean burrito bowl + small shake side | 40 g |
| 9pm | Soy milk with cocoa + handful nuts | 12 g |
| **Total** | | **~153 g** |

---

## Recovery Protocols (All 12 Weeks)

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours, consistent schedule. **Week 11 requires 9 hours.**
- **Mobility:** 10 min daily (hips, t-spine, ankles)
- **Stress management:** 1 yoga/walking session/week
- **Foam rolling/massage gun:** post-training and on Sun
- **Hydration:** ~3 L water + electrolytes around training

---

## Weekly Tracking & Adjustments

**Weekly metrics:**
- Morning bodyweight average (5–7 readings)
- Waist measurement
- 1 progress photo (same lighting, same day)
- Training log (weights, reps, RIR)

**Adjustment rules:**
- Weight gain >0.75 lb/week × 2 weeks → reduce calories by 150
- Weight gain <0.25 lb/week × 2 weeks → add 150 calories
- Lifts regressing 2 sessions in a row → check sleep/food, may need extra rest day
- 2+ overreach signals (resting HR ↑5 bpm, mood drop, joint pain) → pull back intensity

---

## Phase-by-Phase Cardio + Calorie Summary

| Phase | Cardio/Week | Surplus | Daily Calories |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1: Foundation | 55–70 min Zone 2 | +250–300 | ~2,300 |
| 2: Intensification | 80–100 min (Z2 + HIIT) | +300 | ~2,400 |
| 3 (W9–10): Peak | 75–85 min Z2 | +400 | ~2,500 |
| 3 (W11): Peak Week | ~20 min Z2 | +500 | ~2,600 |
| 3 (W12): Deload | 40 min Z2 | +300 | ~2,400 |

---

- **+4–7 lb bodyweight,** lean-tissue dominant
- **+15–25% strength** on squat, bench, RDL, hip thrust
- **Visible hypertrophy** in glutes, quads, shoulders, back
- **Improved work capacity** and aerobic base
- **Established habits:** plant-based protein patterning, training consistency, recovery routine

# 12-Week Integrated Programme: Full Summary

A complete plant-based hypertrophy plan for a 26-year-old vegan recreational female lifter. All components — training, cardio, nutrition, recovery — synchronised across the 12-week arc.

---

## Programme At-A-Glance

| Phase | Weeks | Focus | Sessions/Week | RIR | Weekly Cardio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1: Foundation** | 1–4 | Technique, volume base | 4 (Upper/Lower) | 2–3 | 55–70 min |
| **2: Intensification** | 5–8 | Volume expansion + conditioning | 5 (PPL + UL) | 0–2 | 80–100 min |
| **3: Peak Hypertrophy** | 9–12 | Max intensity, intensifiers | 5 (PPL + UL) | 0–1 | 50–85 min |

**Targets across all 12 weeks:**
- **Bodyweight gain:** +4–7 lb (lean tissue priority)
- **Rate of gain:** 0.25–0.5 lb/week
- **Strength gain:** 15–25% on main compounds
- **Daily protein:** 150 g (plant-based)
- **Daily calories:** 2,300–2,500 (adjusts up to +500 surplus in Phase 3)

---

## PHASE 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

### Training: 4-Day Upper/Lower Split
- **Mon:** Upper A (bench, row, shoulder press, lat pulldown, triceps, biceps)
- **Tue:** Lower A (squat, RDL, lunges, leg curl, calves, abs)
- **Wed:** Rest / Zone 2 cardio
- **Thu:** Upper B (incline DB, chest-supported row, lateral raise, face pull, isolation)
- **Fri:** Lower B (deadlift, leg press, Bulgarian split squat, hip thrust, calves, abs)
- **Sat:** Zone 2 cardio + mobility
- **Sun:** Rest

**Volume:** 3 sets per compound, 2–3 per isolation. RIR 2–3 most weeks.

### Cardio
- Wed: Zone 2, 25–30 min
- Sat: Zone 2, 30–35 min
- 7,000–8,000 daily steps target
- **Week 4 deload:** 2 × 20 min easy

### Weekly Progression
- **W1:** Establish loads, RIR 3
- **W2:** +2.5–5 lb on compounds, RIR 2
- **W3:** Add load again, RIR 1–2
- **W4:** **Deload** — 2 sets per exercise, 60% load, RIR 4

---

## PHASE 2: Intensification (Weeks 5–8)

### Training: 5-Day Push/Pull/Legs + Upper/Lower
- **Mon:** Push (chest, shoulders, triceps) + conditioning finisher
- **Tue:** Pull (back, rear delts, biceps)
- **Wed:** Legs (quad-dominant)
- **Thu:** Rest / Zone 2 cardio
- **Fri:** Upper (hypertrophy focus)
- **Sat:** Lower (glute/ham focus)
- **Sun:** Rest

**Volume:** 3–4 sets per compound, 3 per isolation. RIR 1–2.

### Cardio
- Mon: 5–6 round HIIT finisher (30 sec on / 90 sec off)
- Thu: Zone 2, 30–40 min
- Sat: 20 min Zone 2 cooldown
- Sun: Optional 30–45 min easy walk
- **Week 8 deload:** Drop conditioning, 2 × 20 min Zone 2

### Weekly Progression
- **W5:** New split, RIR 2, introduce conditioning finisher
- **W6:** Add a set to weakest muscle, +1 round on finisher
- **W7:** RIR 0–1 on isolation, +10 min Zone 2
- **W8:** **Deload** — 40% volume cut, 3 sessions, RIR 4

---

## PHASE 3: Peak Hypertrophy (Weeks 9–12)

### Training: 5-Day Split (same structure, max intensity)
- **Mon:** Push (intensifiers)
- **Tue:** Pull (intensifiers)
- **Wed:** Legs — quad focus (cluster sets on squat)
- **Thu:** Rest + 20 min walk
- **Fri:** Upper (rest-pause, drop sets)
- **Sat:** Lower — glute/ham focus (eccentric overload)
- **Sun:** Full rest

**Volume:** 4 sets per compound, 3–4 per isolation. RIR 0–1.

**Intensifiers used systematically:**
- Drop sets (last set of isolations)
- Myo-reps (delts, hams, lats)
- Lengthened partials (delts, hams, biceps, triceps)
- Rest-pause (chest, back)
- Cluster sets (back squat)
- 4-second eccentrics (RDL, incline press)

### Cardio
- Drop all conditioning finishers
- Thu: 30 min Zone 2
- Sat: 25 min Zone 2
- Sun: 30 min easy walk
- **Week 11 peak:** One 20 min walk only
- **Week 12 deload:** 2 × 20 min Zone 2

### Weekly Progression
- **W9:** Introduce intensifiers, RIR 0–1 on isolations
- **W10:** +1 set to two priority muscles (delts, glutes typically)
- **W11:** **Peak week** — every isolation past failure, +500 cal surplus, 9 hr sleep
- **W12:** **Hard deload + retest** — 3 sessions, 50% volume, RIR 4, test 3RMs on key lifts

---

## Nutrition: Full 12-Week Framework

### Daily Targets
- **Protein:** 150 g (~2.3 g/kg) — non-negotiable, anchors the entire plan
- **Carbs:** 280–320 g (scaling up in Phase 3 to ~350 g)
- **Fat:** 65–75 g
- **Calories:** 2,300–2,500 (Phases 1–2), 2,500–2,700 (Phase 3)

### Protein Distribution (4–5 feedings of 30–40 g)

| Meal | Protein | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Breakfast | 35–40 g | Tofu scramble, oats + protein powder, overnight oats |
| Lunch | 35–40 g | Tempeh/tofu + grain bowl, lentil pasta, seitan stir-fry |
| Pre/post workout | 30–40 g | Pea+rice protein shake with banana + oats |
| Dinner | 35–40 g | Tofu/tempeh/seitan + carb + veg |
| Optional snack | 15–20 g | Edamame, soy yogurt, protein shake |

### Core Plant Protein Sources (Daily Rotation)
1. **Soy daily** (tofu, tempeh, edamame, soy milk) — best leucine profile
2. **Seitan** 2–3×/week — highest protein density
